title: Disable the panel by overlay alone in clamshell recovery
author: mkelk
body:
The parser this PR originally added is withdrawn; `docs/clamshell.md` in this PR carries the invariant the command is now written to, and everything below was verified against a real Hyprland in the ISO acceptance VM, not against stubs alone.

Closes #8123. Closes #7498. References #7084 (its `require`d-file half is the maintainer's to place). #7326 and #8103 live in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling` and stay open.

**The bug class.** `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell` disabled the panel with a toggle overlay and a reload — and then also evaluated an explicit `hl.monitor({ … scale = … })` on top, with values read out of `monitors.lua`. That explicit write is the phantom-scaling family: to write the right value the script had to read the config exactly the way Hyprland reads it, and no reader closes that obligation — rules also come from `hyprland.lua`, required files, and the toggles. Three readers were built and reviewed on this PR; every review round found the same defect in a new spelling.

**The change, in four parts:**

1. **Overlay only.** The command authors exactly one thing: `hl.monitor({ output = "<internal>", disabled = true })` in the toggles directory. Enabling is removing it and reloading — Hyprland re-applies its own config, panel included, at whatever scale, position and mode the user configured, wherever they configured it. Nothing reads `monitors.lua`, nothing writes a monitor value. Transitions are atomic (mktemp + rename), one bounded reload each, with byte-exact file-backed rollback and a retry on the next run; an idempotent run creates nothing, not even transiently. The predicates are three-valued — true, false, or unknown — and an unknown is never taken for false, so a hung `hyprctl` cannot re-enable the panel mid-clamshell. The unsafe-name refusal (#8129) is kept, before any effect, and the hosted recoveries run only when the toggle each exists to recover is present.

2. **The lock, made real.** The command takes its own blocking lock, so a lid event queues instead of being dropped (the watcher's `flock -n` skip wrapper goes). Every call that can reach Hyprland is bounded by a timeout that escalates TERM→KILL — a callee that ignores TERM cannot be waited on forever — and the lock descriptor is not lent to those callees, so a surviving descendant cannot keep the lock after the command exits (both failure modes reproduced first). A lock that cannot be taken exits before any effect.

3. **The external predicate, made honest.** `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active` broke its own contract twice. It ended in `jq -e`, whose exit 4 for "no match" made every undocked laptop's "no active external" read as *unknown* — so the manual-toggle wake never fired in production. And it counted `FALLBACK`, the enabled placeholder output Hyprland uses under a reserved name when no real output remains — so a machine whose only display had gone down read as docked, deadening the recovery helpers' own "no external active" guards in exactly the states they exist for. It now answers 0 for an enabled real external, the contracted 1 when a successful query finds none (`FALLBACK` excluded by its exact name), and 2 when the query itself failed. Truthiness callers keep their existing behavior — which still treats unknown like false: a transient query failure while an external is active can still drop a user toggle, a pre-existing residual now stated in `docs/clamshell.md` — while the helpers seeing `FALLBACK`'s truth in their recovery states is a deliberate behavior change.

4. **The stranded panel, repaired deliberately.** A helper killed between removing its toggle flag and its reload — reachable, since `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` bounds this command at 0.4 s — leaves Hyprland holding `disabled = true` with nothing on disk wanting it: with no external monitor, a machine with no usable display. The old command papered over this by accident with its explicit eval; this PR repairs it on purpose. When the overlay is absent, the enable path asks the *compositor* — never the config: a panel reported disabled, with no manual toggle and no active external, gets one reload so the config answers again; a panel that comes back is woken, one the config still reports disabled is not. The answer is not remembered, so while that state persists each reconciliation invocation spends one idempotent reload — a lid event is one invocation, a monitor-change retry chain up to four — and a reload that brings another output up closes the gate instead. Every unknown repairs and wakes nothing, including a query that prints a valid answer and then hangs or fails: the query's status is checked before its output is parsed.

**Measured, not assumed.** `test/acceptance.d/clamshell-test.sh` runs the real command against a real Hyprland (headless outputs standing in for the panel and the external; only the two lid/DRM hardware predicates stubbed). Nine `monitors.lua` shapes round-trip with the panel coming back as it was; a user's own disable rule governs through and out of clamshell; a config Lua rejects reloads "ok" with the error in `configerrors` while the overlay still applies beside it (measured — and asserted); an `auto` position is laid out afresh on each reload rather than restored as a slot (identical under the previous command, so no behavior change); and the repair path is exercised for real — the stranded state staged against Hyprland's actual `FALLBACK` placeholder, with the repair's effects *observed* through a forwarding `hyprctl` wrapper: exactly one real reload per gated run, a wake only for a panel that actually came back.

**Tests.** `test/shell.d/monitor-clamshell-test.sh` is derived from the invariant, not the implementation: T1 asserts the command's text contains no reader and no monitor-value write; P1 runs the real external predicate through its whole contract against a controlled `hyprctl`; T2 makes both transitions under six configs any reader would answer differently and requires identical calls; T3 walks the full transition table with every collaborator stubbed — the 3×3 predicate matrix, byte-exact rollback, lock queueing/refusal/surviving-descendant, every call class hung (TERM-ignoring included), the repair row with each of its gates and the masked-query cases at both steps. Each added case was demonstrated to fail against the code without its fix, and key fixes are mutation-checked. The reader's 413-line scale test is deleted with the reader.

**Stated residuals** (`docs/clamshell.md`): the DPMS wake is best-effort and not retried; a stale disable rule beside a still-active external stands until the next transition or an unrelated reload (the user has a display); a migration removes the now-unwritten `internal-monitor-scale` state file.

+
+Clamshell is a laptop with its lid closed and an external monitor active. Omarchy then disables the internal panel, and enables it again when the lid opens or the external monitor goes away. `bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell` does this; it is run by the lid switch bind in `default/hypr/bindings/utilities.lua`, by `omarchy-system-wake`, and by `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-watch` on every monitor add or remove (with retries at 1, 3 and 7 seconds) and every 2 seconds while docked.
+
+This document is the invariant that command is written to, the assumptions it makes about Hyprland, and how each is tested. A change to the command is checked against this document, not against the previous implementation.
+
+## The overlay
+
+The command manages one thing: an overlay, `~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/internal-monitor-clamshell.lua`, holding one rule:
+
+```lua
+hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", disabled = true })
+```
+
+`default/hypr/toggles.lua` requires every `.lua` file in that directory, so the overlay is part of the config Hyprland reads on reload, alongside `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua` and everything `hyprland.lua` reaches. Disabling the panel is placing the overlay and reloading. Enabling it is removing the overlay and reloading: Hyprland re-applies whatever the config says about the panel, at whatever scale, position and mode the user configured, wherever they configured it.
+
+Nothing else is written. Earlier versions also evaluated an explicit `hl.monitor(...)` for the panel after the reload, with a scale read out of `monitors.lua`, and so needed to read that file the way Hyprland does — an obligation no parser closes, since rules also come from `hyprland.lua`, from required files and from toggles. The compositor is the only reader of its own config, and nothing this command does overrides its answer.
+
+## The invariant
+
+- **I1 — authorship.** The only monitor property the command authors is the overlay above. It never authors geometry (scale, position, mode) and never authors `disabled = false`. The overlay is authored only for a known internal name that is safe to write into Lua and into a `hyprctl` argument (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`); an unsafe name is refused with exit 1 before any effect, and no overlay is ever authored for an empty name.
+
+- **I2 — the transition relation.** The inputs are the internal name (unsafe, unknown, or known), the clamshell condition, and the manual-disable toggle (`internal-monitor-disable.lua`). Each predicate — `omarchy-hw-clamshell`, `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active` — is read as a tri-state: exit 0 is true, exit 1 is false, a timeout or any other status is unknown. Clamshell is their three-valued conjunction: false if either is false, true if both are true, unknown otherwise. An unknown is never taken for false. That reading is only as honest as the predicates' exits (P1): each must answer 0 for true, 1 for its known false, and anything else only when it does not know. `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active` originally ended in `jq -e`, whose exit 4 for "no match" turned every undocked laptop's "no active external" into an unknown — suppressing the manual-toggle wake in production (measured); and it counted `FALLBACK`, the enabled placeholder output Hyprland uses under a reserved name when no real output remains, so the machines in exactly the states the recovery helpers exist for read as docked, deadening those helpers' own guards. It now distinguishes a failed query (unknown, exit 2) from a successful one finding no active external (the contracted exit 1), and never counts `FALLBACK` — deliberately restoring the helpers' stated semantics.

A lock that cannot be taken — the lock file unopenable, or `flock` failing — is a run that must not happen: the command exits 1 before any lookup, helper or transition. Every call inside the lock that can reach Hyprland carries a timeout (`OMARCHY_HYPRCTL_TIMEOUT`, 15 s) that escalates from TERM to KILL, and the lock descriptor is not lent to its bounded callees — the only calls that can outlive the command; the plain file utilities are waited on and spawn nothing — since `timeout` escalates only its direct child, and a surviving descendant would otherwise keep the lock after the command exits: neither a hung compositor, a callee that ignores TERM, nor a callee's leftover descendant can hold the lock. +#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+# The clamshell command's assumptions about Hyprland (docs/clamshell.md, A1-A6),
+# checked against a real one. Two headless outputs stand in for the panel and
+# the external monitor; the two hardware predicates are stubbed, since a VM has
+# no lid; everything that reaches Hyprland is real. Each transition is made by
+# the real command, and the panel must come back as it was: every field the
+# config determines exactly, and an auto position as Hyprland's fresh, but
+# deterministic, layout of the enabled outputs.
+
+internal="eDP-1"
+external="HDMI-A-1"
+monitor_lua="$HOME/.config/hypr/monitors.lua"
+overlay="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/internal-monitor-clamshell.lua"
+expected_overlay="hl.monitor({ output = \"$internal\", disabled = true })"
+
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+stub_bin="$work/bin"
+backup=""
+created=()
+watcher_paused=0
+
+# The lid reads a file the test flips; external monitors are always connected.
+mkdir -p "$stub_bin"
+printf '#!/bin/bash\n[[ $(< "%s/lid") == "closed" ]]\n' "$work" >"$stub_bin/omarchy-hw-laptop-closed"
+printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$stub_bin/omarchy-hw-external-monitors"
+chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*
+printf 'open' >"$work/lid"
+
+output_present() {
+  hyprctl monitors all -j | jq -e --arg name "$1" '.[] | select(.name == $name)' >/dev/null
+}
+
+panel() {
+  hyprctl monitors all -j | jq -c --arg name "$internal" '[.[] | select(.name == $name)] | first // empty'
+}
+
+panel_enabled() { [[ $(panel | jq -r '.disabled') == "false" ]]; }
+panel_disabled() { [[ $(panel | jq -r '.disabled') == "true" ]]; }
+panel_upright() { [[ $(panel | jq -r '.transform') == "0" ]]; }

+snapshot() {
+  panel | jq -c '{scale, x, y, width, height, refreshRate, transform, disabled}'

+    sleep 0.2
+  done
+  return 1

+}
+
+apply_config() {
+  cat >"$monitor_lua"
+  hyprctl reload >/dev/null
+}

+cleanup() {
+  trap - EXIT
+  if [[ -n $backup ]]; then
+    cp "$backup" "$monitor_lua"
+  elif [[ -e $work/config-written ]]; then
+    rm -f "$monitor_lua"
+  fi

+  fi

+  done

+    pkill -CONT -f omarchy-hyprland-monitor-watch >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+  fi
+  rm -rf "$work"

+# predicate, which in a VM answers open; disabling the panel is such an event.
+# It stands still while the test flips the stubbed lid.

+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+# The clamshell command against its invariant (docs/clamshell.md):
+#   I1  it authors one thing, the clamshell overlay, and never a monitor value
+#   I2  a run whose desired overlay state is already on disk changes nothing
+#   I3  one reload per transition, exact rollback on failure, retry next run
+#   I4  every invocation is serialized, nothing is dropped, nothing can hang
+# T1 reads the command's text; T2 shows the config cannot matter; T3 walks the
+# transition relation with every collaborator stubbed and controllable.
+
+command_path="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell"
+
+test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'chmod -R u+w "$test_tmp" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
+
+stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
+home_dir="$test_tmp/home"
+run_dir="$test_tmp/run"
+ctl="$test_tmp/ctl"
+log="$test_tmp/calls.log"
+toggles="$home_dir/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr"
+overlay_file="$toggles/internal-monitor-clamshell.lua"
+manual_flag="$toggles/internal-monitor-disable.lua"
+mirror_flag="$toggles/internal-monitor-mirror.lua"
+monitor_lua="$home_dir/.config/hypr/monitors.lua"
+lock="$run_dir/omarchy-monitor-clamshell.lock"
+bound=1
+
+mkdir -p "$stub_bin" "$toggles" "$home_dir/.config/hypr" "$run_dir" "$ctl"
+
+# Every collaborator is a stub that logs what it was asked and answers as the
+# control directory says: a file named hang-<stub> makes it sleep past the
+# command's bound; stubborn-<stub> makes it ignore TERM while doing so, which
+# only a KILL escalation bounds; fail-<stub> makes it exit 1; odd-<stub> exit 3.
+cat >"$stub_bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf 'hyprctl %s\n' "$*" >>"$OMARCHY_TEST_LOG"
+case $1 in
+  monitors)
+    [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/hang-monitors ]] && sleep 5
+    cat "$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/monitors.json"
+    # A valid answer followed by a failure: the reader must treat the query as
+    # unknown, never as the printed value.
+    [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/slow-monitors ]] && sleep 5
+    [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/sour-monitors ]] && exit 1
+    exit 0
+    ;;
+  reload)
+    [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/hang-reload ]] && sleep 5
+    [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/fail-reload ]] && exit 1
+    # What the config would answer once re-read: repair-flips models a config
+    # that re-enables the panel; repair-slows and repair-sours make the answer
+    # after the reload arrive and then hang, or arrive and then fail.
+    [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/repair-flips ]] && printf '[{"name":"eDP-1","description":"Test Panel","disabled":false,"scale":1.25}]' >"$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/monitors.json"
+    [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/repair-slows ]] && touch "$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/slow-monitors"
+    [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/repair-sours ]] && touch "$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/sour-monitors"
+    exit 0 ;;
+  dispatch) [[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/hang-dispatch ]] && sleep 5; exit 0 ;;
+  *) printf 'hyprctl UNEXPECTED %s\n' "$*" >>"$OMARCHY_TEST_LOG"; exit 1 ;;
+esac
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-laptop" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+printf 'laptop\n' >>"$OMARCHY_TEST_LOG"
+[[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/hang-laptop ]] && sleep 5
+[[ -e $OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/stubborn-laptop ]] && { trap '' TERM; sleep 5 >/dev/null 2>&1; }
+cat "$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/internal"
+SH
+
+# The command's own flock, interposable: fail-flock refuses acquisition, so the
+# refusal path can be walked; otherwise the real flock runs.
+cat >"$stub_bin/flock" <<SH
+#!/bin/bash
+[[ -e \$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/fail-flock ]] && exit 1
+exec $(command -v flock) "\$@"
+SH
+
+for predicate in omarchy-hw-clamshell omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active; do
+  short=${predicate##*-}
+  cat >"$stub_bin/$predicate" <<SH
+#!/bin/bash
+printf '$short\n' >>"\$OMARCHY_TEST_LOG"
+[[ -e \$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/hang-$short ]] && sleep 5
+[[ -e \$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/odd-$short ]] && exit 3
+exit "\$(cat "\$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/$short")"
+SH
+done
+
+# The hosted helpers, stubbed to record their invocation and, when told the
+# toggle is stale, to do what the real one does: drop the flag, reload, wake.
+for helper in internal internal-mirror; do
+  cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-$helper" <<SH
+#!/bin/bash
+printf 'helper $helper %s\n' "\$*" >>"\$OMARCHY_TEST_LOG"
+[[ -e \$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/hang-helper-$helper ]] && sleep 5
+[[ -e \$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/stubborn-helper-$helper ]] && { trap '' TERM; sleep 5 >/dev/null 2>&1; }
+[[ -e \$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/escapee-helper-$helper ]] && { (trap '' TERM; exec sleep 5) >/dev/null 2>&1 & exec sleep 5; }
+[[ -e \$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/fail-helper-$helper ]] && exit 1
+if [[ -e \$OMARCHY_TEST_CTL/stale-helper-$helper ]]; then
+  rm -f "\$OMARCHY_TEST_FLAG_$(tr '-' '_' <<<"$helper")"
+  hyprctl reload >/dev/null
+  hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp.dpms({ action = "enable" })' >/dev/null
+fi
+exit 0
+SH
+done
+
+chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*
+
+expected_overlay='hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", disabled = true })'
+stale_overlay='hl.monitor({ output = "OLD-1", disabled = true })'
+
+# The default state is a known panel, lid open, an external active, no toggles
+# and no overlay: a run with nothing to do. Cases adjust it with prep strings.
+reset_state() {
+  chmod -R u+w "$toggles" 2>/dev/null || true
+  rm -rf "$ctl" "$toggles"
+  mkdir -p "$ctl" "$toggles"
+  : >"$log"
+  printf 'eDP-1\n' >"$ctl/internal"
+  printf '1\n' >"$ctl/clamshell"
+  printf '1\n' >"$ctl/active"
+  printf '[{"name":"eDP-1","description":"Test Panel","disabled":false,"scale":1.25}]' >"$ctl/monitors.json"
+  rm -f "$monitor_lua"
+  printf 'hl.monitor({ output = "", mode = "preferred", position = "auto", scale = 1.25 })\n' >"$monitor_lua"
+}
+
+clamshell() { printf 0 >"$ctl/clamshell"; printf 0 >"$ctl/active"; }
+no_name() { : >"$ctl/internal"; }
+stale() { printf '%s' "$stale_overlay" >"$overlay_file"; }
+
+run_command() {
+  local status=0
+  HOME="$home_dir" \
+    PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
+    XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$run_dir" \
+    OMARCHY_TEST_LOG="$log" \
+    OMARCHY_TEST_CTL="$ctl" \
+    OMARCHY_TEST_FLAG_internal="$manual_flag" \
+    OMARCHY_TEST_FLAG_internal_mirror="$mirror_flag" \
+    OMARCHY_HYPRCTL_TIMEOUT="$bound" \
+    "$command_path" >/dev/null 2>&1 || status=$?
+  return $status
+}
+
+count_calls() { grep -c "^$1" "$log" || true; }
+reloads() { count_calls 'hyprctl reload'; }
+dispatches() { count_calls 'hyprctl dispatch'; }
+evals() { count_calls 'hyprctl eval'; }
+helper_calls() { count_calls 'helper'; }
+
+overlay_equals() {
+  [[ -f $overlay_file ]] && [[ $(< "$overlay_file") == "$1" ]]
+}
+
+listing() { ls -liA --time-style=full-iso "$toggles"; }
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- T1: the text
+
+! grep -qE 'hyprctl[[:space:]]+(eval|keyword)' "$command_path" || fail "T1: the command does not write monitor values with hyprctl eval or keyword"
+! grep -qE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_./-])(awk|gawk|lua|lua5\.[0-9])([^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|$)' "$command_path" || fail "T1: the command invokes no reader (awk or lua)"
+! grep -q 'monitors\.lua' "$command_path" || fail "T1: the command does not name the config file"
+verbs=$(grep -oE 'hyprctl[[:space:]]+[a-z]+' "$command_path" | awk '{print $2}' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
+for verb in $verbs; do
+  case $verb in monitors|reload|dispatch) ;; *) fail "T1: hyprctl verb $verb is not one of monitors, reload, dispatch" ;; esac
+done
+grep -q 'flock' "$command_path" || fail "T1: the command serializes itself with a lock"
+pass "T1: the command's text authors nothing but the overlay and reads no config"
+
+# ------------------------------- P1: the external-active predicate's contract
+
+# The tri-state reading is only as honest as the predicates' exits: 0 true,
+# 1 known false, anything else only for a genuine unknown. The real predicate
+# is run against a controlled hyprctl: the query succeeding with no active
+# external is the contracted false, the query failing is never taken for it,
+# and Hyprland's reserved FALLBACK placeholder is never a monitor.
+p1_ctl="$test_tmp/p1-ctl"; p1_bin="$test_tmp/p1-bin"
+mkdir -p "$p1_ctl" "$p1_bin"
+cat >"$p1_bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+[[ -e $P1_CTL/fail ]] && exit 1
+cat "$P1_CTL/out"
+SH
+chmod +x "$p1_bin/hyprctl"
+p1_case() {
+  local expect="$1" label="$2" got=0
+  P1_CTL="$p1_ctl" PATH="$p1_bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active" >/dev/null 2>&1 || got=$?
+  (( got == expect )) || fail "P1 ($label): exit $expect" "got $got"
+}
+printf '[{"name":"eDP-1","disabled":false},{"name":"HDMI-A-1","disabled":false}]' >"$p1_ctl/out"
+p1_case 0 "an enabled external is true"
+printf '[{"name":"eDP-1","disabled":false}]' >"$p1_ctl/out"
+p1_case 1 "only the internal panel is the contracted false"
+printf '[{"name":"eDP-1","disabled":false},{"name":"HDMI-A-1","disabled":true}]' >"$p1_ctl/out"
+p1_case 1 "a disabled external is the contracted false"
+printf '[]' >"$p1_ctl/out"
+p1_case 1 "no outputs listed is the contracted false"
+printf '[{"name":"eDP-1","disabled":true},{"name":"Virtual-1","disabled":true},{"name":"FALLBACK","disabled":false}]' >"$p1_ctl/out"
+p1_case 1 "the FALLBACK placeholder beside disabled outputs is not an external"
+printf '[{"name":"eDP-1","disabled":true},{"name":"FALLBACK","disabled":false},{"name":"HDMI-A-1","disabled":false}]' >"$p1_ctl/out"
+p1_case 0 "a real enabled external beside FALLBACK is still true"
+printf 'not json' >"$p1_ctl/out"
+p1_case 2 "an unreadable answer is unknown"
+: >"$p1_ctl/out"
+p1_case 2 "an empty answer is unknown"
+touch "$p1_ctl/fail"
+p1_case 2 "a failing query is unknown, never false"
+rm -f "$p1_ctl/fail"
+pass "P1: the external-active predicate answers 0, 1, or unknown -- and a failure is never false"
+
+# ------------------------------------------------- T2: the config cannot matter
+
+# Both transitions are made under configs that any reader would answer
+# differently: the panel at another scale, no file, a file that cannot be read,
+# one Lua rejects, and one that answers by whether it runs in a sandbox. The
+# calls to Hyprland are the same under every one of them.
+t2_calls() {
+  reset_state
+  [[ $2 == enable ]] && stale || clamshell
+  case $1 in
+    plain) ;;
+    other) printf 'hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", mode = "preferred", position = "auto", scale = 2 })\n' >"$monitor_lua" ;;
+    absent) rm -f "$monitor_lua" ;;
+    unreadable) chmod 000 "$monitor_lua" ;;
+    rejected) printf 'local x = (\n' >"$monitor_lua" ;;
+    adversarial) printf 'local seen = os ~= nil\nhl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", position = seen and "left" or "0x0", scale = seen and 3 or 1.25 })\n' >"$monitor_lua" ;;
+  esac
+  run_command || fail "T2: the $2 transition runs with a $1 config"
+  grep '^hyprctl' "$log" || true
+}
+for transition in enable disable; do
+  baseline=$(t2_calls plain "$transition")

+    [[ $(t2_calls "$kind" "$transition") == "$baseline" ]] || fail "T2: the $transition transition makes the same calls with a $kind config" "$baseline"
+  done
+  (( $(reloads) == 1 && $(evals) == 0 )) || fail "T2: the $transition transition is one reload and no written value" "$baseline"
+done
+pass "T2: the config's content cannot matter, since the command never reads it"
+
+# ---------------------------------------- T3: the transition relation (I2, I3, I4)
+
+# Rows of the relation, from both starting states.
+for start in absent stale; do
+  prime() {
+    reset_state
+    [[ $start == stale ]] && stale
+    eval "$1"
+  }
+  untouched_after() {
+    if [[ $start == stale ]]; then overlay_equals "$stale_overlay"; else [[ ! -e $overlay_file ]]; fi
+  }
+
+  # unsafe name: refuse before any effect
+  prime 'printf "eDP-1; rm -rf x\n" >"$ctl/internal"; clamshell; touch "$manual_flag" "$mirror_flag"'
+  ! run_command || fail "T3 ($start): an unsafe internal name is refused with exit 1"
+  untouched_after || fail "T3 ($start): an unsafe name leaves the overlay untouched"
+  (( $(reloads) == 0 && $(dispatches) == 0 && $(evals) == 0 && $(helper_calls) == 0 )) || fail "T3 ($start): an unsafe name causes no effect, and the helpers are not entered"

+  # unknown name + clamshell: untouched
+  prime 'no_name; clamshell'
+  run_command || fail "T3 ($start): unknown name in clamshell runs"
+  untouched_after || fail "T3 ($start): unknown name in clamshell leaves the overlay untouched"
+  (( $(reloads) == 0 && $(dispatches) == 0 )) || fail "T3 ($start): unknown name in clamshell reloads and dispatches nothing"
+
+  # unknown name, not clamshell: absent, one reload, no wake
+  prime 'no_name'
+  run_command || fail "T3 ($start): unknown name out of clamshell runs"
+  [[ ! -e $overlay_file ]] || fail "T3 ($start): unknown name out of clamshell leaves no overlay"

+  untouched_after || fail "T3 ($start): the manual toggle leaves the overlay untouched"
+  (( $(reloads) == 0 && $(dispatches) == 0 )) || fail "T3 ($start): the manual toggle in clamshell reloads and dispatches nothing"
+
+  # known + clamshell: exact overlay, one reload; again: nothing
+  prime 'clamshell'
+  run_command || fail "T3 ($start): clamshell runs"
+  overlay_equals "$expected_overlay" || fail "T3 ($start): clamshell writes exactly the overlay"
+  (( $(reloads) == 1 && $(dispatches) == 0 && $(evals) == 0 )) || fail "T3 ($start): clamshell reloads exactly once and writes no value"

+  (( $(reloads) == 0 && $(dispatches) == 0 )) || fail "T3 ($start): clamshell with the overlay in place does nothing"

+
+  # known, not clamshell: absent, one reload, one wake
+  prime ':'
+  run_command || fail "T3 ($start): out of clamshell runs"
+  [[ ! -e $overlay_file ]] || fail "T3 ($start): out of clamshell leaves no overlay"
+  if [[ $start == stale ]]; then
+    (( $(reloads) == 1 && $(dispatches) == 1 )) || fail "T3 (stale): leaving clamshell reloads once and wakes once"

+    (( $(reloads) == 0 && $(dispatches) == 0 )) || fail "T3 (absent): out of clamshell with no overlay does nothing"
+  fi
+done
+pass "T3: every row of the relation from both starting states"
+
+# The wake guard on the enable path: manual toggle on, external active / not / unknown.

+  reset_state; stale; touch "$manual_flag"
+  if [[ $active == hang ]]; then touch "$ctl/hang-active"; printf 1 >"$ctl/active"; else printf "$active" >"$ctl/active"; fi

+  [[ ! -e $overlay_file ]] && (( $(reloads) == 1 )) || fail "T3: enable with manual toggle removes the overlay and reloads once (active=$active)"

+done
+pass "T3: the wake guard treats unknown as active"
+
+# The 3x3 predicate matrix, overlay present and stale, name known.

+  for ext in 0 1 2; do
+    reset_state; stale

+      p=${pair%%:*}; v=${pair##*:}

+    done
+    run_command || fail "T3 matrix ($lid,$ext): runs"
+    if (( lid == 1 || ext == 1 )); then
+      [[ ! -e $overlay_file ]] && (( $(reloads) == 1 && $(dispatches) == 1 )) || fail "T3 matrix ($lid,$ext): a known false is not clamshell: overlay removed, one reload, one wake"

+      overlay_equals "$stale_overlay" && (( $(reloads) == 0 && $(dispatches) == 0 )) || fail "T3 matrix ($lid,$ext): unknown leaves the overlay untouched"
+    else
+      overlay_equals "$expected_overlay" && (( $(reloads) == 1 )) || fail "T3 matrix (0,0): clamshell rewrites a stale overlay and reloads once"
+    fi
+  done
+done
+pass "T3: the three-valued conjunction: false dominates, unknown suspends, both true is clamshell"
+
+# Rollback is byte-exact, from a file, never synthesized.
+for trailing in 0 3; do
+  reset_state; clamshell; touch "$ctl/fail-reload"
+  { stale; for ((i = 0; i < trailing; i++)); do printf '\n'; done >>"$overlay_file"; }

+  run_command || fail "T3 rollback ($trailing newlines): runs"
+  cmp -s "$overlay_file" "$test_tmp/prior" || fail "T3 rollback ($trailing newlines): a failed reload puts back the exact prior bytes"
+  (( $(reloads) == 1 )) || fail "T3 rollback ($trailing newlines): one reload attempt"
+  rm -f "$ctl/fail-reload"; : >"$log"
+  run_command || fail "T3 rollback ($trailing newlines): the next run runs"
+  overlay_equals "$expected_overlay" && (( $(reloads) == 1 )) || fail "T3 rollback ($trailing newlines): the next run retries the transition"
+done
+reset_state; no_name; stale; touch "$ctl/fail-reload"; cp "$overlay_file" "$test_tmp/prior"
+run_command || fail "T3 rollback (unknown name): runs"
+cmp -s "$overlay_file" "$test_tmp/prior" || fail "T3 rollback (unknown name): the enable side puts back the exact prior bytes"
+! grep -rq 'output = ""' "$toggles" || fail "T3 rollback (unknown name): no overlay for an empty name is ever written"
+rm -f "$ctl/fail-reload"; : >"$log"; run_command || true
+[[ ! -e $overlay_file ]] && (( $(reloads) == 1 )) || fail "T3 rollback (unknown name): the next run removes the stale overlay"
+pass "T3: rollback restores the exact prior bytes and the next run retries"
+
+# No debris, both sides, including a directory that cannot be written.
+for side in place remove; do
+  reset_state
+  if [[ $side == place ]]; then clamshell; else stale; cp "$overlay_file" "$test_tmp/prior"; fi
+  chmod 555 "$toggles"
+  run_command || fail "T3 read-only ($side): runs"
+  if [[ $side == place ]]; then [[ ! -e $overlay_file ]] || fail "T3 read-only (place): no overlay appears"; else cmp -s "$overlay_file" "$test_tmp/prior" || fail "T3 read-only (remove): the overlay stands byte-for-byte"; fi
+  (( $(reloads) == 0 && $(dispatches) == 0 )) || fail "T3 read-only ($side): a transition that cannot be made attempts no reload and no wake"
+  chmod 755 "$toggles"
+  [[ $(ls -A "$toggles" | grep -v '^internal-monitor-clamshell.lua$' | wc -l) -eq 0 ]] || fail "T3 read-only ($side): no debris"
+done
+reset_state; clamshell; mkdir "$overlay_file"
+run_command || fail "T3 directory: a directory at the overlay's path runs"
+[[ -d $overlay_file && -z $(ls -A "$overlay_file") ]] && (( $(reloads) == 0 )) || fail "T3 directory: a directory at the overlay's path is left as it is, with nothing in it, and no reload" "$(ls -lA "$toggles" "$overlay_file")"
+[[ $(ls -A "$toggles" | wc -l) -eq 1 ]] || fail "T3 directory: no debris beside it"
+pass "T3: a transition that cannot be made is not attempted and leaves nothing"
+
+# A killed run's debris -- the EXIT trap does not run on SIGKILL -- is swept
+# under the lock by the next run that passes name validation, before either
+# hosted helper can end that run early.
+reset_state; clamshell; printf 'orphan' >"$toggles/.internal-monitor-clamshell.tmpXYZ"; printf 'old bytes' >"$toggles/.internal-monitor-clamshell.prior.XYZ123"
+run_command || fail "T3 sweep: runs over a killed run's debris"
+[[ ! -e $toggles/.internal-monitor-clamshell.tmpXYZ && ! -e $toggles/.internal-monitor-clamshell.prior.XYZ123 ]] || fail "T3 sweep: the debris is gone" "$(ls -A "$toggles")"
+overlay_equals "$expected_overlay" && (( $(reloads) == 1 )) || fail "T3 sweep: the run's own transition still happens"
+reset_state; printf 'orphan' >"$toggles/.internal-monitor-clamshell.prior.ABC456"

Force-pushed. The PR now also reads a rule whose output names a local (reported by @jelenv on #6909) — the same reader missing a rule for the same reason as the multiline case, so it belongs here rather than in a fourth PR. Rebased onto current `quattro`.

Body updated with the new case, the test list (35 assertions, was 30), and how this sits against the other open monitor work: #7581, #7000 and #7505 all merge clean with this in either order, and the suite is green on the merged trees — verified, not assumed.

Reviewed on a disposable worker against `quattro` at c539f03. `quattro` has moved since this branch was cut — #7581 landed as b6361642 — so I reviewed the merge rather than the branch alone. It merges clean, and on the merged tree `monitor-clamshell-scale-test.sh` is 40 ok, with `monitor-recovery`, `monitor-state`, `monitor-scaling`, `monitor-modeless`, `lid-close` and `sleep-lock` green and `./test/cli` green.

Beyond the suite I ran this script and the current `quattro` one side by side over about three dozen fixture configs, comparing the `hyprctl eval` each would write. The forms that already worked still work: the shipped `monitors.lua`, a plain single-line connector rule, a trailing line comment, a commented-out decoy, a `desc:` full of regex metacharacters, a description containing `/`, a paren inside a double-quoted description, a malformed rule missing its closing paren, and the leave-`auto`-alone path #7581 added. The new forms read correctly too, including last-rule-wins across `desc:`/connector pairs and the nwg-displays multiline shape.

Three regressions, one root cause: `strip_comments` and `depth_of` are not string-aware, so a Lua string can open a fold that swallows the rest of the file.

**1. A `(` inside a single-quoted Lua string.** `depth_of` (:95) strips only `"…"`, so the paren counts as structure, the rule never closes, and the catch-all is folded into it.

```lua
hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", position = "0x0", scale = 1.25, icc = '/profiles/panel(warm.icc' })
hl.monitor({ output = "", position = "auto", scale = 1 })
```

`quattro` applies `scale = 1.25, position = "0x0"`. This branch applies `scale = 1, position = "auto"`.

**2. A `--` inside a double-quoted value.** `strip_comments` (:80) truncates there, which removes the closing `)`, with the same consequence.

```lua
hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", position = "0x0", scale = 1.25, icc = "/profiles/panel--warm.icc" })
hl.monitor({ output = "", position = "auto", scale = 1 })
```

Same before and after as above. Escaped `\"` is the same class. On my fixtures both only bit when the panel's own rule was the one truncated — a swallow that starts on a rule *before* it leaves the panel's keys last on the joined line and reads correctly by luck.

**3. `--[==[` is not recognised as a long comment** (:83), only `--[[`. That was harmless before, because a multiline rule inside one could not be folded and was ignored for that reason. Now it can be, so a commented-out rule becomes live.

```lua
--[==[
hl.monitor({
  output = "eDP-1",
  scale = 3,
})
]==]
hl.monitor({ output = "", position = "auto", scale = 1.25 })
```

`quattro` reads 1.25. This branch reads 3.

One smaller thing, not a regression. `internal_monitor_output` trims the selector with `read` (:190), matching Hyprland, but `configured_monitor_value` then looks the rule up by the trimmed spelling. `output = "desc:Samsung Display Corp. "` with a trailing space is identified as the panel's rule and then cannot be read, so it falls to the catch-all — the same outcome as today, just a case the new matcher gets halfway.

And one on the tests: `write_block_commented_rule_config` does not discriminate. `quattro` also reads 1.25 there, because it cannot fold the multiline rule inside the comment. The body lists it among the fixtures confirmed to fail unpatched.

Checked and not findings, for the record: the escaping in `monitor_rule_regex` holds up against `desc:` selectors containing `[](){}.*+?^$|/\`; `lua_local_value` returning 1 propagates nowhere, since the script sets neither `-e` nor `pipefail`; and the extra parsing costs about 4 ms per invocation on the 2-second poll, which I do not think matters, though `INTERNAL_OUTPUT` is now computed before the clamshell-disable branch that never reads it.

Second opinion from `codex` at xhigh. It found the single-quote and `--[==[` cases, which I had not reasoned about, and the `icc` framing that makes them concrete; I verified all three by running both scripts. Two of its variants do not hold — a single-quoted paren or an escaped quote on an earlier rule reads correctly, for the reason above — and a fourth, a `desc:` selector matching only Hyprland's raw description, is the residual your body already documents, which falls back exactly as today. @omarchybot All three confirmed and fixed, along with rather more that pulling on them turned up. The branch is rebased onto `quattro` at 2c247e39 and force-pushed.

## Your three

Reproduced exactly as you described, so I started where you pointed: making the fold pass string-aware. One character-scanning walk tracking quoted strings with their escapes, and long brackets at any level, replaced `strip_comments` and `depth_of` — they need identical string awareness, so one scanner emitting stripped text and a depth delta is smaller than the two of them, not larger. `--[==[` falls out for free once long brackets are understood rather than pattern-matched, and the same walk covers long *strings* used as values.

I also took your smaller item — `internal_monitor_output` trimmed the selector with `read` and then looked the rule up by the trimmed spelling, so `output = "desc:Samsung Display Corp. "` was identified and then not findable. `IFS= read` keeps the spelling; only the description a `desc:` name carries is trimmed, which is what Hyprland trims.

And you were right about `write_block_commented_rule_config`. It used a *multiline* rule inside the comment, which `quattro` cannot fold and therefore also reads correctly — the fixture discriminated nothing and the body claimed otherwise. A single-line rule inside `--[[ ]]` does discriminate, and that is what it uses now.

## What that turned up

Fixing the fold made it obvious the same blindness lived in the other readers, and further review found it did:

- **A name the config rebinds between rules.** `lua_local_value` took the first `local` in the file, so `local mon = "eDP-1"` … `mon = "DP-2"` pointed *both* rules at the panel and the panel got DP-2's scale and position, reapplied every 2 seconds. Declaring one variable and reusing it per monitor block is a normal way to write that config, which made this the worst of the lot.
- **A key merely ending in `output`.** `monitor_rule_outputs` had no key-boundary guard and matched greedily, so `mirror_output = "DP-2"` hid the rule's real output and the panel fell to the catch-all. Same mechanism for rule-shaped text inside a quoted value.
- **A backslash-continued string.** Lua carries a short string past the end of its line; the scanner did not, so a rule written inside such a string was read as a live rule. `lua5.1` with a stubbed `hl` confirms the config means one thing and the script read another.
- **A multiline scale expression.** After folding, `scale = scale_for(\n 2880\n)` extracted as *empty*, which read as a rule naming no scale, so the catch-all overruled a panel Hyprland was scaling correctly — the exact flap the delegate guard from #7581 exists to prevent.

Every one of those is a regex that cannot see where a string begins, where a key ends, or what order the file is in. Patching them individually would have left the next shape unreadable, so the reader is now one pass: `scan_monitor_config` walks the config once and emits only what the rest needs — which output each rule addresses, and what it says about scale and position. Rules are matched by comparing that output as text, so nothing is escaped into a regex any more. `resolve_rule_outputs`, `monitor_rule_regex`, `monitor_rule_outputs`, `monitor_rules`, `join_monitor_rules` and `lua_scalar` are gone.

That also closed shapes neither of us had flagged as broken: `{output = name}` with no space after the brace (the local-keyed feature silently no-opped there), the table brace on the next line, `hl.monitor { }` without call parens, single-quoted strings in a rule rather than only in a binding, and a name bound twice now taking the later binding as Lua does. And an empty `desc:` selector: `starts_with("")` is true, so Hyprland applies such a rule while the script skipped it — the script and the compositor disagreeing about which rule governs the panel, which is the one thing this reader must not do.

In fairness the rewrite introduced one of its own on the way, caught before it settled: the gate deciding whether a line held a monitor call was still a plain regex, so an unrelated table whose string happened to mention `hl.monitor(` and which carried rule-shaped keys was read as a rule. It is a string-aware walk now, with a fixture.

## On the tests

Your point about non-discriminating fixtures generalised. A mutation pass found two more guards covering nothing: deleting the regex escaping from `monitor_rule_regex` entirely passed all 49 assertions, and so did removing the empty-`desc:` guard. The escaping is moot now — text comparison has nothing to escape — but the replacement is mutation-tested: swapping it for a glob comparison kills a fixture carrying `?`, `*`, `[` and `.`.

Your "last rule matching the panel wins" fixture had the same shape of problem I had missed: it put the `desc:` rule *first*, an order `quattro` also passes because it ignores `desc:` rules and lands on the connector rule anyway. Connector-first is the order that distinguishes last-match-wins from connector-always-wins, and there is now a fixture for it.

The suite is 63 ok, up from 25. Every new assertion was checked to fail against the version before the fix it guards, by running the suite with a non-fatal `fail` against each ancestor commit rather than by assuming.

## On your last two notes

The ~4 ms you measured was on configs without local-keyed outputs. With them the cost multiplied — the config was scanned once per lookup and again per name, 42 times per invocation on a twelve-monitor config, about 194 ms every 2 seconds. Reading it once makes that flat: 21 ms there against 19 ms for the shipped config, both at or below `quattro`.

And `INTERNAL_OUTPUT` is computed on the branch that reads it now. You were right that the clamshell-disable branch never touches it, and that branch is the one the docked poll takes.

## Verification

`./test/shell` is 182 of 188 files green, with the same six failing identically on an unmodified checkout for local system-state reasons. `./test/cli` green, and `monitor-recovery`, `monitor-state`, `monitor-scaling`, `monitor-modeless` and `lid-close` green. Differentially against `quattro` over the fixture battery: every already-working shape byte-identical, and every difference a case this PR exists to fix, checked against a `lua5.1` oracle where the answer was not obvious.

Worth another look — the fix is a good deal larger than what you reviewed.

Re-reviewed at 68c8e095 on a disposable worker, against `quattro` at 19266119 — it has moved two commits since your rebase, neither touching these files, and GitHub reports the merge clean.

## The block-assignment trade

You framed it as binary: take the assignment, or delete the binding. We took a third path — not every block is a condition, so the tracker keeps block *kinds* rather than a count. An assignment inside a `do` or `repeat` body has run and binds; inside a function body it has not run where it is written, and does not; inside an `if` or a loop body it is unknowable, and the name is left unreadable so the rule using it falls back to the compositor. That keeps the reads the flat delete would have lost, and it caught a shape neither of us had filed: a helper function assigning to a name the rules below use no longer rebinds it.

Codex then completed it in the direction your comment pointed — "the same mechanism reaches the output name." A name marked unknowable now makes a rule whose *output* rests on it emit as *unresolved* (`U`), and any unresolved rule makes the panel's rule ambiguous, because it could address the panel and could be the last match. Recovery then acts on nothing: the docked poll delegates to the compositor, whose answer is definitionally right, and re-enable uses the scale the panel last ran at. The same restraint now covers a whole `hl.monitor` call inside a branch or a function — a rule that may not exist and a rule that may be anything ask the same thing of the reader. `quattro` reads a rule out of a never-called function and applies it two writes a second; that one was ours to find, not yours, and it is fixed at `db1149f4` with both gate directions mutation-killed.

One honest cost: any output the scanner cannot resolve — `"DP-" .. n`, say — now delegates the whole config where `quattro` applied the catch-all. Safe direction, but a behavior change on a plausible shape, and yours to veto.

## The lock can be held by a descendant the timeout never reached

The stale-lock question comes out well: this is an `flock` on an inherited fd, not a lockfile with a PID check, so it is released on death. But fd 9 is inherited by every descendant, and GNU `timeout` only escalates to KILL while its *direct* child is still alive. Measured on the test VM (coreutils 9.11): a helper that dies on TERM while a backgrounded TERM-ignoring grandchild keeps running makes `timeout --kill-after=1` exit 124 without ever escalating; the grandchild survives, and `flock -n` on the lock file reports it **still held** after the command's shell has exited. A `setsid`/`setpgid` descendant escapes the same way. Since `flock 9` blocks with no deadline, that wedges every later run and the lid-switch bind with it.

Nothing in the current chain does either — `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-{laptop,internal,internal-mirror,external-active}`, `omarchy-hyprland-toggle`, `hyprctl` and `jq` all read clean — so this is the gap between the code and I4's "neither a hung compositor nor a callee that ignores TERM can hold the lock", and `stubborn_case` only covers a TERM-ignoring direct child. It closes categorically, without depending on signal semantics, by not lending the descriptor out at all:

```bash
bounded() {
  timeout --kill-after=1 "${OMARCHY_HYPRCTL_TIMEOUT:-15}" "$@" 9>&-
}
```

Smaller, same area: `exec 9>"$LOCK"` failing is fail-closed today — bash continues, `flock 9` fails with `EBADF`, the command exits 1, all confirmed — but not if the command ever inherits an already-open fd 9, since the failed redirection leaves that descriptor intact and `flock 9` would lock the wrong file. `exec 9>"$LOCK" || exit 1` costs nothing.

**Pushed one commit, `dcd744de`.** `test/acceptance.d/clamshell-test.sh:337` asserted only that the predicate answers false in the staged state, which reads identically whether Hyprland ran its placeholder or stopped making one — so the case advertised as real-Hyprland `FALLBACK` coverage could have passed with no `FALLBACK` row ever existing. It now asserts the row. Renaming what the new helper looks for makes the case fail, so it is not vacuous, and the whole file still passes 17/17 on the VM. Codex found this one.

**One medium is open, and it is not yours — it predates this PR.** `disable_internal` returns at `:131-133` whenever the desired overlay is already on disk byte-for-byte, so a run killed between the rename at `:101` and the reload at `:138` leaves the overlay written and Hyprland never told. Staged on the VM — exact overlay on disk, clamshell true — the command makes two `hyprctl monitors` calls, zero reloads, and the panel stays `disabled: false`: the panel is lit behind a closed lid, and every later clamshell run does nothing about it. It clears on the next lid open→close cycle or any unrelated reload, so it costs battery and light rather than a display. `bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock:89` is what makes it reachable, the same 0.4 s bound `docs/clamshell.md` already cites for the helper case, and the base branch has the same shape at its own `disable_internal:239`. Worth saying plainly: the re-review at `aef12949` told you this side "converges", and that was wrong. Not pushed, because closing it means either dropping I2's idempotence (a reload every 2 s on the docked poll) or asking the compositor on the disable path the way `repair_disabled_panel` does on the enable path — a `hyprctl monitors` added to the hot poll and a new row in the I2 table. That is your call, not a reviewer's.

**Three smaller things.** The `EXIT` trap at `:85` does not run on `SIGKILL`, so `omarchy-system-sleep-lock`'s `--kill-after=0.1s` leaves the `keep_prior` copy behind — measured: after `SIGTERM` the toggles directory is clean, after `SIGKILL` it holds `.internal-monitor-clamshell.prior.unGTjH`. `default/hypr/require_all.lua:18` globs `*.lua`, so Hyprland never loads it and nothing breaks, but nothing removes it either. Second, `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal:54` and `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal-mirror:59` read the predicate for truthiness, so the new exit 2 is still taken for the contracted false and a transient query failure can drop the user's toggle while an external is up — not a regression, since the old `jq -e` exited 4 both when the query failed and when it found nothing (measured), but P1 is the argument for making the predicate honest and these are the two callers that cannot yet benefit; `tri` is the pattern. Third, the repair's gate opens only on a compositor-disabled panel, so the mirror half of the killed-helper story has no repair by construction — `docs/clamshell.md` scopes transactional helper recovery out, and it would read more honestly if it said the repair covers the disable case only.

**Not a finding, but worth knowing:** if a `monitorremoved` event is ever missed, the docked 2 s poll keeps running with no external active, and a config-disabled panel then enters the repair every two seconds and spends a reload each time. `sync_poll_state` stops the poll on every monitor event and treats an unknown predicate as false, so this needs a genuinely dropped event — but before the repair existed a stuck poll cost nothing, and now it costs a reload every 2 s. Codex raised it; the trigger is a pre-existing gap in the watcher, not something this PR introduces.

**What ran, and where.** On the VM: `test/shell.d/monitor-clamshell-test.sh` (15/15), `monitor-output-name-test.sh` (8/8), `monitor-recovery-test.sh` (18/18), `lid-close`, `sleep-lock`, `monitor-modeless`, `sleep-monitor`, `./test/cli` (116/116), and the whole `./test/shell` suite at 2852 passed. Five unrelated files fail on that VM — `ascii`, `branding-about-animation`, `screenshot-sanity`, `theme-install-guards`, `windows-vm-mount-boundary` — and they fail identically on `21b27c5a`, so they are the VM, not this branch. `test/acceptance.d/clamshell-test.sh` was run against the VM's real Hyprland and passes 17/17 including the repair cases; the round-trip and `FALLBACK` results above come from that run and from staging the states by hand.

**Where codex landed.** It confirmed the head and all three anchors, and it contributed two things this review had not reached on its own: the vacuous `FALLBACK` assertion, now fixed, and the poll-amplification note above. It also reached the disable-path skip independently. Its other claim — that the two truthiness callers are made destructive by the new exit 2 — does not hold as a regression, for the reason measured above. Its independence is not currently guaranteed, since a read-only sandbox still lets it read this session's own transcript; nothing in its log suggests it did.

Waiting on you for the disable-path skip, and on the maintainer for #8808, which is a competing implementation in the same file — it teaches the reader `desc:` and multi-line rules where this PR withdraws the reader altogether. #7501 is not a collision: it touches `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling` and the SDDM greeter, shares no file with this branch, and nothing outside the deleted code ever read the `internal-monitor-scale` state that `migrations/1787996352.sh` removes.

Answered at `ebd47f66`, on top of your `dcd744de` — thanks for that one; the vacuous assertion was real, and the strengthened case is exactly right.

**The SIGKILL debris is swept.** Any `.internal-monitor-clamshell.*` file found at the start of a run is a killed run's leftover — under the lock no live run owns one — and is removed by the next run that passes name validation, before either hosted helper can end that run early (the unsafe-name refusal rightly stays first). The focused test plants both kinds and requires them gone on a transitioning run, a no-op run, and a run a failing helper cuts short; removing the sweep or moving it after the helpers each fail the cases that name them.

**The disable-path skip: accepted, stated, and deliberately not closed.** You're right that "converges" was wrong for this side, and the residual is now stated plainly in `docs/clamshell.md`: a run killed between placing the overlay and its reload leaves the desired bytes with Hyprland never told, and later runs do not reload — lit panel behind a closed lid until the next lid cycle or any reload from elsewhere. It predates this PR, self-heals, and costs light rather than a display. The straightforward closure — the disable-path analogue of the repair — would put a `hyprctl monitors` query on every docked 2 s poll and is declined rather than grow this PR again; a durable pending-reload marker cleared after a successful reload is another possible design (more transaction state, a possible harmless duplicate reload), also not taken up here. The doc names both.

**The mirror half named honestly**: the docs now say the repair covers the disable toggle's residual only — its gate opens on a compositor-disabled panel, and a killed mirror helper leaves none.

**The two truthiness callers**: agreed, and now stated in the tracked doc rather than only conceded here — both recover helpers read the predicate as plain truthiness, so their behavior is unchanged, but it still treats unknown like false: a transient query failure while an external is active can still remove the user's toggle. Not a regression (your exit-4 measurement matches ours: the old predicate behaved the same), and the tri-state read is the pattern when it is taken up; it touches two other commands and is out of this PR's scope. The PR body's "truthiness callers are unaffected" is corrected to say exactly this.

The poll-amplification note is noted as what it is — a pre-existing watcher gap that now has a small new cost attached; nothing in this PR relies on the poll surviving a missed event.

I took the hosted-helper residual already called out in `docs/clamshell.md` and exercised it against this exact head (`ebd47f66`). There are two small pieces here, one expected and one I did not expect.

1. Both recovery helpers still read `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active` as ordinary truthiness. With this PR's new contract, exit `2` is *unknown*, but:

* `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal recover`
* `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal-mirror recover`

both currently let that unknown reach the same path as the contracted false. A transient failed monitor query can therefore remove the user's disable/mirror toggle even though the external display may still be active.

2. The internal recovery helper also masks a failed mutation. It does:

```bash
omarchy-hyprland-toggle $TOGGLE off
wake
```

and `wake()` is best-effort (`... || true`). If removing the toggle fails, the successful wake becomes the function's exit status, so this PR's caller (`recover ... || exit 0`) cannot enforce the documented "failed hosted helper stops before the clamshell branch" transaction boundary. The mirror helper already propagates its toggle failure.

I put the narrow follow-up on top of this PR head here:

https://github.com/kvnloo/omarchy/commit/ef16db7550c05dd772910ccd05c459f130ce0db2

The behavioral fixture drives both helpers with external-active statuses **0 / 1 / 2 / 124** and an injected toggle-removal failure. Only `1` is allowed to mutate; unknown/timeout are no-ops; a failed mutation stays nonzero; and the internal helper does not wake after that failure. 10 focused assertions pass in the isolated harness.

I kept it separate because the tri-state residual is explicitly out of scope here, but the status-masking half intersects this PR's stated helper-failure invariant directly. Happy for either/both pieces to stay follow-up work if that keeps this branch narrower.
